title: INDIAN AIR FORCE CONCLUDES HIGH-TEMPO MULTINATIONAL EXERCISES PITCH BLACK AND UDARA SHAKTI 2026
body_text:
The Indian Air Force (IAF) has successfully concluded its participation in two pivotal international flight engagements: Exercise Pitch Black 2026 in Australia and Exercise Udara Shakti 2026 in Malaysia. The dual-nation deployment underscored the IAF’s operational reach, advanced tactical coordination, and commitment to strengthening strategic defence partnerships across the Indo-Pacific region.
During Exercise Pitch Black 2026, hosted by the Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF), the IAF deployed its frontline Rafale aircraft to operate alongside Air Forces from over 20 participating nations. Executing complex Large Force Employment (LFE) missions in a high-threat, multi-domain environment, the exercise enabled seamless tactical integration, cross-learning, and enhanced interoperability among coalition partners.
Following the operations in Australia, the IAF contingent deployed directly to Subang, Malaysia, for Exercise Udara Shakti 2026. IAF aircrew executed high-intensity combat sorties and joint tactical manoeuvres alongside the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), flying with and against Su-30MKM and F/A-18 Hornet aircraft. The bilateral engagement focused on refining air combat tactics, subject matter expert exchanges (SMEE), and optimizing combined operational flexibility.
Throughout both deployments, joint operations extended beyond the cockpit to include maintenance practices, mission planning exchanges, and cultural interactions, bolstering professional camaraderie across ranks.
The Indian Air Force remains dedicated to enhancing regional stability, fostering interoperability, and advancing collaborative security initiatives through continuous joint training engagements across the global defence community.
***
JS/VK/SM

enrichment.summary: The Indian Air Force concluded participation in two multinational exercises: Pitch Black 2026 in Australia, hosted by the Royal Australian Air Force with over 20 nations, where IAF Rafale jets conducted Large Force Employment missions; and Udara Shakti 2026 in Subang, Malaysia, a bilateral exercise with the Royal Malaysian Air Force involving combat sorties against Su-30MKM and F/A-18 Hornet aircraft. Both exercises aimed to enhance interoperability, tactical coordination, and strategic defence partnerships across the Indo-Pacific.
enrichment.context:
India has increasingly used multinational and bilateral air exercises as instruments of defence diplomacy to deepen ties with Indo-Pacific partners amid growing strategic competition in the region, particularly involving China. Exercise Pitch Black, a biennial multinational exercise hosted by Australia, has become a significant platform for India to showcase its Rafale fleet and integrate with air forces from countries like the US, Japan, France, and Southeast Asian nations. Udara Shakti, a bilateral exercise with Malaysia, reflects India's 'Act East' policy and efforts to build interoperability with ASEAN air forces operating diverse platforms such as Russian-origin Su-30s and American F/A-18s.

Such exercises, while not policy announcements themselves, are part of India's broader strategy of enhancing military diplomacy, projecting power-sharing capabilities, and building coalition-level readiness. They also serve to test indigenous and imported platforms like the Rafale in complex, high-threat, multi-domain scenarios alongside allied nations.
